children: The three main U.S. federal banking regulators issued an interim final rule that would allow more banks to qualify for fewer exams of their businesses, the latest in a series of victories that bank lobbying groups have notched under the Trump administration.

On Thursday, the Federal Reserve Board, Federal Deposit Insurance Corp., and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said jointly that more community banks would be eligible for an 18-month exam cycle instead of a 12-month cycle.

"The extended cycle applies to small banks with relatively low-risk profiles, but the agencies would continue the current supervisory practice of offsite monitoring between scheduled exams," the three agencies said in a statement.
